thread:
maria (oncall): incident-bot paging — high GPU saturation observed in us-west pools. alert: gpu_pool_util >= 95% for 3m. queue depth climbing.

incident-bot: AUTO: page sent to #incidents @oncall — gpu_pool_util=97% queue_len=920 avg_token_latency=320ms spike. severity: P1.

kevin (runtime): seeing huge KV-cache warmup after v9.8 rollout started at ~3790012200. Prefill traffic is exploding. logs show repeated large context preloads.

emma (sre): confirm impact: customer-facing latencies up, some 502s. Are any critical customers impacted? @olivia can you surface any support pings?

olivia (support): multiple paid customers reporting timeouts for embeddings and chat in us-west. MRR customers: 3 active threads. Ticket numbers: #CS-5421, #CS-5423. They're seeing 5-10s latencies and occasional 504.

raj (infra): autoscaler not responding as expected. max_replicas capped at 20, current_replicas=20, queue_len=1200. autoscale_events show multiple throttle decisions: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:10Z scale_request -> denied (max_replicas)
2026-03-15T14:03:05Z scale_request -> denied (quota)
```

kevin (runtime): digging into model metrics: v9.8 introduced a change to kv-lookup prefetch logic. For long contexts it pre-warms many KV shards per request. Median kv_reads/request up 6x. That explains memory/IO bloat and CPU saturating GPU hosts.

emma (sre): can we throttle prefill at runtime? Flag exists: `runtime.prefill.enabled` and `runtime.max_prefill_tokens`.

kevin (runtime): yes, can flip a flag from console or via config rollout. Suggest immediate soft-disable of prefill: set `runtime.prefill.enabled=false` for rollout-v9.8 route.

maria (oncall): do it now — we need guardrails while we mitigate autoscaler limits. @kevin, do you want me to take the action or you?

kevin (runtime): I'll push a temporary route config patch, but need someone to watch GPU pools. Steps: 1) disable prefill on v9.8 routes 2) lower per-request kv_shard_prefetch to 2 3) open emergency capacity if needed. Patch ready.

kevin (runtime): applying patch now:
```
# patch
route: v9.8
runtime.prefill.enabled: false
runtime.kv_shard_prefetch: 2
```

deploy-bot: deploy started for config-change v9.8-prefill-off by kevin at 2026-03-15T14:08:12Z

emma (sre): rolling watchers on GPU pool metrics and queue. @raj, any room to temporally raise max_replicas?

raj (infra): escalation path: we can raise cluster quota for 30m and spin additional GPU nodes, but provisioning ~4 extra pools will take ~5-7 minutes. I'll request emergency increase now and bump autoscaler max to 40 to absorb the burst.

raj (infra): raised quota request in cloud console, submitted. Also temporarily set autoscaler.max_replicas=40 for us-west pools.

incident-bot: NOTICE: autoscaler.max_replicas updated -> 40 by raj at 2026-03-15T14:10:04Z

kevin (runtime): metrics after flag flip (14:11): queue_len dropping from 1200 -> 420 over 3m, avg_token_latency falling 320ms -> 160ms, gpu_pool_util trending down 97% -> 82%. Looks promising but still unstable.

emma (sre): are we still seeing 502/504?

olivia (support): errors decreasing but some customers still report retries. I'll update CS tickets: informing customers we're mitigating and investigating root cause.

maria (oncall): what about KV memory pressure? Any spillovers to disk causing OOMs?

kevin (runtime): kv-cache memory per-pod spiked. Some pods spilled to node-level tmpfs and caused evictions in two hosts. I marked those pods for restart. We'll need a followup to evaluate prefetch heuristics.

raj (infra): extra nodes are provisioning now. I see 6 new GPU nodes entering cluster, autoscaler distributed pods. No further evictions since 14:16.

kevin (runtime): for postmortem: v9.8 changed kv prefetch threshold inadvertently. We'll revert the rollout once we stabilize. For now: disable prefill, lowered prefetch, increased autoscaler cap, restarted evicted pods.

emma (sre): customer impact summary for incident timeline to include in incident report: 14:02 alerting begins; 14:08 prefill disable; 14:10 autoscaler cap increase; 14:17 stable trend. Impact: elevated latencies 14:02–14:17, intermittent 502/504s, majorly affecting us-west hosted endpoints for customers using long-context requests.

olivia (support): drafted customer message: "We're investigating a runtime regression after a model rollout causing increased warmup traffic and latency in US-West. We've applied mitigations and are monitoring. Some customers may experience degraded latencies for up to 30 minutes. We will follow up with root cause and timeline."

maria (oncall): assign followups: 1) kevin — full rollback plan and PR to revert v9.8 prefetch change; 2) raj — autoscaler tuning and guardrails to prevent immediate max cap explosions; 3) emma — incident writeup + customer impact summary; 4) ops — run canary of fixed behavior in staging.

kevin (runtime): filing rollback PR and feature-flag patch: #PR-7812. Also adding stronger limits to prefetch logic: cap per-request kv_reads to 8 and additional throttling when pool_util > 85%.

raj (infra): will add policy: autoscaler should not breach customer-impact threshold without pause and human approval. Also adding an alert for queue_len growth > 500 while pool_util > 85%.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated (P1 -> P2) at 2026-03-15T14:25:00Z. Continue monitoring; postmortem required.

emma (sre): good work. Keeping channel open for 30m for verification. I'll start the postmortem doc and assign timeline entries. :thumbsup:

olivia (support): sending customer updates now. Will attach incident link when doc ready.

maria (oncall): handing off to emma for postmortem and to raj/kevin for followups. Oncall clear in 30m if stable.

kevin (runtime): note for postmortem: add unit test for prefetch heuristics + integration test that simulates long-context cold starts to avoid regression.

emma (sre): last check at 14:34: queue_len=48 gpu_util=64% avg_latency=140ms error_rate=0.6%. Marking this thread as 'monitoring -> handback' at 3790012600.

maria (oncall): thanks all.
